name: Toy ruleset
description: The fast unit-test ruleset. Its constants are the original's confirmed values, transcribed from the reports in the research repository's docs/reports/ and cited per field in the sibling "_provenance" blocks; its flags are set the way the shipped classical-faithful preset sets them. It exists so tests do not depend on the full classical-mediterranean world, which task T29 exports separately.

_provenance.earlyLateWeekThreshold: confirmed: decompiled-weather-events.md — Spring's 'early'/'late' boundary is week < 6; Autumn's is week < 7 (the report gives the two seasons different boundaries, not the same one). Represented here as a single field because on this engine's odd-week calendar (weeks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) the two readings pick out exactly the same set of weeks either way, so a single shared threshold of 6 is behaviourally equivalent to carrying 6 and 7 separately (review round 1, B5). Summer and Winter are flat for the whole season, so their early/late split never matters.

The table's per-type shooting-vulnerability weight (+0x20, read for the target's type: light infantry 18, heavy infantry 2, archers 18, light cavalry 15, heavy cavalry 4) is now each row's shotVulnerability [confirmed: 2026-10-04-decompiled-tactical-battle-rules.md §4 for the tactical shot formula's use; the field's identity is earlier — battle-replayed-rout-mechanic-and-combat-constants.md identified +0x20 as the shooting vulnerability, and unit-type-stat-table-in-dat.md carries an Update saying the same]. The shipped instant resolver never reads it; the tactical battle (docs/game-design.md §Combat) does.
_provenance.archerUnitTypeId: confirmed: original unit type code 2 is the archer type, IC2.Data.UnitCatalog maps it to the id 'archers' [decompiled-unit-map-orders-and-record-fields.md — "archers counted ×3", type table "Ar 3,500"]. The pointer itself is [designed]: nothing in UnitTypeRules marks a type as the one the siege formula triples (Shots/Range describe the tactical shell this build does not have, and deriving "archer" from them would invent a rule), so T54 searched the whole of this record for an existing pointer field, found none, and carried the id as a call-site constant (BattleCommandRuleset.ArcherUnitTypeId) instead (bug #221 N1). T66 adds this field so the id lives in ruleset data like every other constant; both shipped rulesets and Armies/ArmyNaming's canonical type list already agree on 'archers'.
